title: Galois restriction isomorphisms give equivalences of abelian etale sheaves
statement: Let $K\hookrightarrow L$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension], with compatible separable closures $K^s\hookrightarrow L^s$ [def-kun-separably-closed]. Let $e:\operatorname{Gal}(L^s/L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Gal}(K^s/K)$ be an isomorphism of topological groups for their Krull topologies, satisfying $e(\sigma)(x)=\sigma(x)$ after inclusion into $L^s$. Then the existing inverse-image functor $u^{-1}:\operatorname{Ab}((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}})\to\operatorname{Ab}((\operatorname{Spec}L)_{\mathrm{et}})$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], where $u=\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow L)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], is an equivalence. This assertion concerns all abelian sheaves and requires neither valuations nor torsion.

proof.text: Replace both closures by isomorphic separable closures in the universe of the ground fields. Transport the inclusion through the isomorphisms. Conjugation identifies the Krull topologies, because inverse images of pointwise stabilizers of finite intermediate fields are precisely stabilizers of their transported finite intermediate fields. This transports e and its restriction formula. Choose an algebraic closure Omega of the small Ls and compose all field embeddings into it.

proof.text: Apply the abelian Galois-stalk equivalence to each field with this common geometric overfield Omega, retaining the action-normalization clauses. The field-pullback/Galois-action theorem, with these clauses, supplies a natural isomorphism from the actual inverse-image functor followed by the L stalk equivalence to the K stalk equivalence followed by restriction along e.

proof.text: Restriction along e has inverse restriction along e inverse. On objects these functors keep the underlying integral module and change its action by composition; on morphisms they keep the underlying maps. Stabilizers pull back to open stabilizers under both continuous maps. The unit and counit are identities of underlying modules, with equivariance given by the inverse identities for e. Hence restriction is an equivalence. The two stalk functors are equivalences, so transport across the natural comparison and cancel the L stalk equivalence to conclude that the actual inverse image is an equivalence.

theorem upperStar_isEquivalence_of_galoisRestriction
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    (Ks : Type s) (Ls : Type t) [Field Ks] [Field Ls]
    [Algebra K Ks] [IsSepClosure K Ks]
    [Algebra L Ls] [IsSepClosure L Ls]
    [Algebra Ks Ls] [Algebra K Ls]
    [IsScalarTower K Ks Ls] [IsScalarTower K L Ls]
    (e : Gal(Ls/L) ≃ₜ* Gal(Ks/K))
    (he : ∀ (σ : Gal(Ls/L)) (x : Ks),
      algebraMap Ks Ls (e σ x) = σ (algebraMap Ks Ls x)) :
    (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))).IsEquivalence
